A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLVE/RLVE-GYM work. Their main text, nine figures, Table 1, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–E are readable and complete enough for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL training experiments, adaptive-versus-static comparisons, environment-scaling analyses, and six-benchmark evaluations, including appendix Figures 8–9.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and benchmark results in Sections 4–5 and appendix Figures 8–9.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same environment sampling, performance-triggered difficulty updates, sliding window, and DAPO training procedure. Shortened explanations do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RLVE-GYM environments and held-out tasks, plus AIME 2024/2025, OMEGA-500, OlympiadBench, LiveCodeBench, and BBEH. No evaluated domain or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same static-difficulty alternatives, continued original ProRL training, and RLVR on DeepMath-103K. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices C–E retain the same model initializations, training settings, environment splits, 4,000-problem ID and 2,500-problem OOD evaluations, and Avg@64/Avg@4/Pass@8 metrics.

E4.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the Sorting and Multiplication case studies, adaptive-versus-static comparisons, and scaling analysis using 1, 4, 16, and 256 environments. No robustness, sensitivity, or error analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version introduces repeated-training seed statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The result curves and findings in Figures 3–9 are unchanged, including the appendix breakdowns. Section 5.1 retains the reported gains of 3.37 percentage points for RLVE and 0.49 for continued original RLVR; the DeepMath-103K comparison is also unchanged.

T1.justification: The environment definitions, difficulty-update equations, configurable-difficulty reasoning, and appendix reward formulas are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the paper retains its claims about adaptive difficulty, generalization through environment scaling, and compute-efficient reasoning improvements. Caption revisions restate claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: The explanations of saturation, learning efficiency, and generalization remain substantively unchanged. Section 7 reorders the existing discussions of non-verifiable environments and automatic environment engineering; the new generic Impact Statement adds no specific limitation.

D1.justification: Appendices A–E retain the same hyperparameters, environment specifications, training and evaluation configurations, hardware, runtime information, and environment lists. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bao et al.'s algorithmic-reasoning work, DataEnvGym, EvalTree, and DR Tulu, while removing SimpleRL-Zoo. Section 6 modestly broadens the adaptive-data discussion to capability-tailored SFT without redefining RLVE's central positioning.

P1.justification: v2 selectively condenses prose and captions, shortens the model-stage explanation, and reverses the two future-work discussions. It also adds an Impact Statement and conference publication text; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The same figures and table remain, with caption formatting and wording changes. Figure 2 changes columns, Figure 6 moves from page 8 to page 7, and surrounding text reflows. The plotted content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides modestly fuller scholarly context by acknowledging algorithmic-problem training in Section 3.1 and connecting adaptive data to capability-tailored SFT in Section 6. These are limited improvements in attribution and positioning; the method, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
